items.claim: A refused WGSL pipeline still draws until the async refusal arrives, voiding that first pass
items.note: question. Neither way out is a fix I could make here. `createRenderPipelineAsync`, or holding draws until validation settles, would drop the first-use draws of every program, kit programs included. Then a static scene would never show them, because nothing asks for a repaint. The voided frame can only be repainted once the renderer has a way to ask its host for a redraw. Which of these to build is a design call. `refusedProgram.browser.test.ts` already accepts the first-frame void.

items.claim: WebGPU targets report the requested `samples`/`bytes`, not what was allocated
A straight-alpha `ImageBitmap` with `premultiply: false` is premultiplied on WebGPU
items.note: question. Nothing reports whether a bitmap's alpha is premultiplied, so WebGPU can't match GL's "as held" for both kinds of bitmap. `premultipliedAlpha: data.premultiply` fixes the reported case but breaks parity for default (premultiplied) bitmaps. Someone has to rule what `premultiply: false` means for a bitmap.
